test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The supermarket may declare a weekend offer for all the food items.

options.text: A weekend offer may have been declared by the supermarket for all the food items.
A weekend offer would be declared by the supermarket for all the food items.
A weekend offer may be declared by the supermarket for all the food items.
A weekend offer may declare by the supermarket for all the food items.

solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in **active voice **and in the modal structure with **'may'.**
 
• When such sentences are transformed into passive voice, they follow the structure **'Modal + be + past participle' **for the new verb phrase.
 
• Hence, "The supermarket may declare a weekend offer for all the food items" transforms into "A weekend offer may be declared by the supermarket for all the food items".

Therefore, the correct answer is - **Option 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ability to use modal verbs correctly within passive structures — such as can, could, may, might, should, among others — are crucial for English learners.
 
• Other options do not follow the correct use of modal verbs in passive voice. 
 
 
• For example, **'have' in option 1 **can only be used for perfect forms, **'would' in option 2 **is the past of **'will', and option 4 **incorrectly uses 'may declare' instead of 'may be declared'.
